reason: Start recovering iron from worn red cells so the marrow can reuse it.
expectation: The recycling cells will break down worn red cells and make their iron available, though I don't know exactly what form it will take.

alternatives.reason: Growing replacement skin cells is also a goal, but I want to follow the iron route first.

effect: The recovered iron is carried in blood, so I can follow it to the marrow.
reaction: It makes sense that the recycling cells remain intact; the protein carriers were a useful detail.
reason: Use the recovered iron in the marrow to continue the red-cell replacement goal.
expectation: The marrow will use the iron to help make new red blood cells, though I’m not sure if another step will be needed.

alternatives.reason: Skin replacement is also a goal, but I want to finish following the iron first.

effect: The recovered iron is now in new red cells, completing that goal; skin replacement remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the iron reused while the marrow's stem cells remain.
reason: This is the only available combination and follows the remaining skin-cell goal.
expectation: The dividing skin cells will use the supplied materials to grow replacement cells.

effect: The skin result completes the remaining goal and shows new cells replacing shed surface cells while the base population remains.
reaction: The continuous layer and shedding flakes made replacement easy to picture.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following recovered iron into new red blood cells was worthwhile because it showed what gets reused and where it goes.

leastWorthwhile.text: The skin-cell combination was clear but less engaging as a decision because it was the only available action.

surprise.text: The recovered iron travels in blood on protein carriers rather than as metal fragments.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless; both pairings followed the stated replacement goals, though compatibility was supplied by the menu.

continue.text: I might continue for another chapter if it connects familiar body processes in a similarly clear way, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
